label: Mountain
_model: Wild kernel at altitude. The appetite belongs to the hill — it wants to be gone up, to be cold, to be the only way through, and to have everything come to rest at its foot. Claimants are the mountain's own names, and its cruelties are all things weather does anyway.

appetites.want: to be gone up and not come down from
appetites.purpose: everything that went up would stay up
appetites.asks: "Is that as high as you're going?"

appeasement.move: go up one stretch you did not have to

appetites.want: never to have anything warm on it
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be comfortable up here

appeasement.move: go without your fire for a night, on purpose
appeasement.why: it was cold and you bore it

appetites.want: that nothing should get past it without asking
appetites.purpose: every crossing would come through it
appetites.asks: "And where do you think you're going?"

appeasement.move: ask the pass for leave, aloud, before you go through

appetites.want: that everything should come down to it and stay
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be taken away again

appeasement.move: put something down and leave it where it falls

accommodations.text: kept {conscript} at the top, facing out, where they can still be seen
let {conscript} go up in good weather and did not let them down in it
took {conscript}'s warmth a finger at a time until they stopped noticing
came down on {conscript} in the night, all at once
closed the pass behind {conscript} and did not open it again
made a landmark of {conscript}, which travellers still steer by

cairn.label: the topmost stone of the summit cairn
cairn.function: the only proof anybody ever got all the way up

fire.label: the fire that stayed lit above the snowline
fire.function: the only warm thing this hill ever allowed

waystone.label: the waystone from the top of the pass
waystone.function: the only thing that ever said which way was through

stone.label: the stone that stopped rolling
stone.function: the only thing here that ever came to rest of its own accord

factions.name: the Left
factions.essence: went up and are still up, and are past minding about it

factions.name: the drovers
factions.essence: were taking stock over the pass when it closed

factions.name: the cold itself
factions.essence: is not hunting you and will kill you anyway

factions.name: what walks above the snowline
factions.essence: has never been down and does not intend to be

triggerGlossary.announced: came up the path in daylight, where the whole hill can see you
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: skylined twice on the same ridge
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice on a slope with snow above it
triggerGlossary.lingering: stopped moving long enough for the cold to start working
triggerGlossary.disturbed: took a stone off a cairn, crossed a cornice, or lit a fire above the snowline

skirmish.line: 2 Dire Wolves on the lower slopes

foes.name: Dire Wolf
foes.note: work you downhill, away from the path

skirmish.avoid: get above them and they will not come up at you

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: one push and you are off the ridge — Poise 1 or fall

fight.avoid: it holds the ridge and nothing else; the scree slope below is open the whole way

battle.line: 1 Troll in the gully and 2 Dire Wolves above it

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: REGENERATES 2 Grit a round unless the wound was burnt

foes.name: Dire Wolf
foes.note: hold the top of the gully

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire touches it — say so before initiative, and there is no fuel above the snowline
battle.avoid: it will not leave the gully; the buttress is longer and it is climbable

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith above the snowline, 1 Troll and 3 Dire Wolves

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit; the cold is already doing that

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest, fire for the Troll
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open and shelter within a Turn

ascent.dangerLine: the hill takes everything that goes up and it has never once had to come and get it

institution: a path that only goes one way and does not branch
cairns set at every point where you might doubt the route
a summit that is visible from everywhere and reached from nowhere
ritual: a stone carried up and added to the cairn at the top
a rest taken at the same rock each time by everyone who goes
boots turned to face downhill when you stop
demand: a cairn one stone short and a flat stone beside it
a path going up with nothing coming down it
boots left turned to face uphill
wound: cairns pushed over in a line all the way to the top
a path worn deep in one direction only
a rest-rock with everything on it that somebody was carrying
anchor: the topmost stone of the summit cairn
a route description that reaches the top and back
a path that goes down as well as up

features: a cairn one stone short
boots turned to face uphill
a rest-rock with a pack still on it
cairns pushed over in a line
a path worn deep one way
a flat stone set ready

decisions.cue: a cairn one stone short with a flat stone laid ready beside it
decisions.cost: adding it finishes somebody else's climb

resolve.success: you place the stone and the route ahead is marked all the way, both directions
resolve.failure: you take a stone instead and the route unmarks itself behind you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it short; the cairns stop being where you remember them

decisions.cue: boots left turned to face uphill at a rest place
decisions.cost: they are turned downhill by anyone intending to go home

resolve.success: you turn them down and whatever wore them can go, and tells you what it saw
resolve.failure: you turn yours uphill to match and the hill counts you among the ones going up
resolve.orElse: leave them; the rest place is not a place you can rest

decisions.cue: a path worn deep in one direction and unworn in the other
decisions.cost: everybody came up this and nobody went down it

resolve.success: you find the descent route that was actually used, which is not this one
resolve.failure: you plan to go down the way you came and the way is not there
resolve.orElse: accept it; every route from here is committed, and the hill knows

decisions.cue: a rest-rock with a pack still on it and the straps done up
decisions.cost: somebody sat down and went on without it

resolve.success: you go through the pack and learn how far they thought they had to go
resolve.failure: you shoulder the pack and the hill treats you as the one who left it
resolve.orElse: leave it; you carry your own weight and it tells at the top

decisions.cue: cairns pushed over in a line all the way up
decisions.cost: somebody unmade the route on purpose, going up or coming down

resolve.success: you work out which direction they were going and what they were stopping
resolve.failure: you rebuild them and everything that uses the route comes back to it
resolve.orElse: leave them flat; nothing will find you up here, including help

decisions.cue: a route description that reaches the top and describes the way back down
decisions.cost: the descent half is the valuable half

resolve.success: you read it and can get off the hill from anywhere on it
resolve.failure: you read only the ascent and are on the summit with no way described down
resolve.orElse: leave the paper; the top is the easy part and you have not read the hard part

situations.doing: carrying a stone uphill with both hands
situations.onArrival: it stops and offers you the stone
situations.because: the cairn is one short and it has been carrying this a long time
situations.offer: take the stone up for it and it will show you the way down

situations.doing: sitting on a rest-rock with the stock long gone
situations.onArrival: he asks whether the pass is open above
situations.because: he came up to take them over and never got word
situations.offer: tell him the pass and he will point out every safe line on the face

situations.doing: standing turned to face uphill at a windbreak
situations.onArrival: they are dry inside and there is frost on the laces
situations.because: they are turned downhill by anyone meaning to go home
situations.offer: turn them down and whoever wore them speaks, and answers you

situations.doing: standing on the skyline facing outward
situations.onArrival: they turn together as you come onto the ridge
situations.because: they were kept at the top facing out, so travellers could see them
situations.offer: stand between them once and every route off this hill opens to you

situations.doing: running up past you with nothing at all coming down it
situations.onArrival: the ground is worn a hand's depth in one direction
situations.because: everything went up and the hill kept it
situations.offer: go up willingly and it will let you come back down

situations.doing: standing one stone short on a false summit
situations.onArrival: the flat stone beside it has been placed ready and not set
situations.because: somebody was finishing the route and stopped here
situations.offer: set the stone and the true summit shows itself

temptations.cue: the topmost stone off the summit cairn
temptations.benefit: once, be counted as having got to the top
temptations.standingDrawback: the hill considers the top unmarked while you have it

temptations.cue: a route description with the descent on it
temptations.benefit: get off this hill from anywhere
temptations.standingDrawback: it is written for weather you do not have

temptations.cue: a dead climber's boots, dry
temptations.benefit: once, go up ground you could not
temptations.standingDrawback: they go up more readily than they come down

temptations.cue: an abandoned pack, still full
temptations.benefit: once, have what somebody prepared for
temptations.standingDrawback: they prepared for a night you have not had yet

temptations.cue: a flat stone cut for a cairn
temptations.benefit: once, mark a route so it stays marked
temptations.standingDrawback: everything that reads cairns follows it too

cold.dangerLine: the cold is not hunting anybody and it will still have all of you by morning

institution: a snowline that does not move all year
bothies built every few miles because the gaps kill people
ground that is frozen a spade deep in every season
ritual: a fire laid in every bothy by whoever leaves it
dry wood carried up and never burnt on the way
hands checked at every stop, each of the party in turn
demand: a bothy with the fire laid and no one to light it
dry wood stacked above the treeline where none grows
frost forming on the inside of something
wound: bothies with the doors off and the fires long cold
wood burnt all at once in a single night
frost on the inside of a shelter that was occupied
anchor: the fire that stayed lit above the snowline
a bothy that has never been let go out
dry wood that does not run out

features: a fire laid but unlit in a bothy
dry wood stacked above the treeline
frost on the inside of a wall
a door off a shelter
ash from a single great burning
hands going white at a stop

decisions.cue: a bothy with the fire laid and nobody there to light it
decisions.cost: lighting it is warm and visible for miles

resolve.success: you light it and the party is warm, and the Left come in politely rather than otherwise
resolve.failure: you light it and everything cold on this hill knows exactly where you are: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: sleep cold; -1 die on everything for the next area

decisions.cue: dry wood stacked neatly above the treeline where none grows
decisions.cost: somebody carried it up and did not burn it

resolve.success: you find who carried it and why they were saving it, and it matters
resolve.failure: you burn it and whatever it was being saved for happens anyway, without fuel
resolve.orElse: leave the stack; there is nothing to burn between here and the top

decisions.cue: frost forming on the inside of a shelter that is occupied
decisions.cost: the cold is getting in, or something cold is already in

resolve.success: you find the way it is getting in and can shut it, and the shelter holds
resolve.failure: you assume it is weather and sleep, and wake with one of you colder than the rest
resolve.orElse: stay out of the shelter; the night is spent moving, and costs a Turn

decisions.cue: ash from a great burning where somebody used everything at once
decisions.cost: they burnt it all in a single night and had a reason

resolve.success: you read the ash and learn what they were keeping off, and how well it worked
resolve.failure: you scatter it and what was kept off comes back to the same place
resolve.orElse: leave the ash; you camp there anyway and find out the hard way

decisions.cue: a bothy door lying off its hinges in the snow
decisions.cost: hanging it takes time and makes the place usable

resolve.success: you hang the door and the bothy is shelter again — one safe rest for the delve
resolve.failure: you hang it badly and it comes in on you in the night
resolve.orElse: leave the door; there is no shelter on this side of the hill

decisions.cue: hands going white at a stop, and one of you not saying so
decisions.cost: the cold has already started and somebody is hiding it

resolve.success: you catch it in time and can keep everybody moving and whole
resolve.failure: it goes unsaid and that person loses 1 max Grit for the rest of the delve
resolve.orElse: stop and warm up properly, costing a Turn while the light goes

situations.doing: standing with the fire laid and the door pulled to
situations.onArrival: the kindling is dry and there is frost on the inside of the walls
situations.because: whoever laid it went out and did not come back
situations.offer: light the fire and the Left will come in and talk rather than take

situations.doing: sitting against a wall with frost on the inside of its coat
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you would mind shutting the door
situations.because: it sat down out of the wind and never got up
situations.offer: shut the door and it will tell you where the wood is cached

situations.doing: stacking dry wood above the treeline, load by load
situations.onArrival: she asks whether you have come for it
situations.because: she has been carrying it up for a fire that was never lit
situations.offer: help her carry and she will show you every bothy on the hill

situations.doing: filling a still, clear night with no wind at all
situations.onArrival: your breath stops showing while you stand there
situations.because: it is not hunting anybody and it will have you anyway
situations.offer: give up your fire for the night and it will let you through the high ground

situations.doing: standing at a fire with no fuel in it
situations.onArrival: they hold their hands out over nothing at all
situations.because: the fire went out and nobody put it back
situations.offer: light anything at all in the grate and both will guide you to the pass

situations.doing: spreading on the inside of a shelter while you watch
situations.onArrival: it forms fastest on the wall you came in by
situations.because: the cold gets in somewhere and nobody found where
situations.offer: find the gap and the shelter holds for as long as you need

temptations.cue: an ember off the fire that stayed lit
temptations.benefit: once, be warm anywhere on this hill
temptations.standingDrawback: everything cold up here can see it burning

temptations.cue: dry wood that does not run out
temptations.benefit: fuel wherever you are
temptations.standingDrawback: somebody carried it up for a purpose you are spending

temptations.cue: a dead climber's coat
temptations.benefit: the cold works on you slower
temptations.standingDrawback: it works on whoever you took it from faster

temptations.cue: the key of a locked bothy
temptations.benefit: one guaranteed shelter
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever else needs the shelter comes to the door

temptations.cue: a knack for reading the frost
temptations.benefit: know when the cold is about to turn
temptations.standingDrawback: you know, and you cannot always act on it

pass.dangerLine: the pass is the only way through and it has views about who uses it

institution: a single notch in a ridge that runs forty miles either way
waystones set the whole length of the crossing, in sight of each other
a hospice at the top for the people the crossing catches
ritual: leave asked of the pass, out loud, before setting foot in it
a stone touched at every waystone going through
the crossing made before noon or not at all
demand: a waystone with the next one not visible from it
a pass standing open with nothing moving in it
a hospice door open and the bell rope hanging
wound: waystones thrown down along the whole crossing
a pass closed by a fall and the fall not cleared
a hospice with the door barred and the bell cut down
anchor: the waystone from the top of the pass
a bell that carries the whole length of the crossing
a line of stones you can always see the next of

features: a waystone with no next one visible
a hospice bell rope hanging
a fall of rock across the way
stones thrown down in a line
a door barred from inside
a track going in with none coming out

decisions.cue: a waystone with the next one not visible from it
decisions.cost: the line is broken and the crossing is committed either way

resolve.success: you find the next stone by dead reckoning and the whole line comes back into sight
resolve.failure: you press on by guess and are somewhere the stones do not go
resolve.orElse: turn back down; the pass is not crossed and the ending is on the far side

decisions.cue: a hospice with the door open and the bell rope hanging
decisions.cost: ringing it calls whoever keeps the hospice

resolve.success: you ring properly and are given shelter, and told what is on the crossing
resolve.failure: you ring it and something answers that is not the keeper: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go past; you cross in whatever weather comes, unwarned

decisions.cue: a fall of rock lying across the way with old boots under it
decisions.cost: clearing it opens the pass for everything, both ways

resolve.success: you clear a line through and the pass is open — the drovers can get out, and will help
resolve.failure: you bring the rest of the slope down and the pass is shut for good: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: climb over the fall; the pass stays closed behind you and nothing follows, including help

decisions.cue: waystones thrown down along the whole crossing, deliberately
decisions.cost: somebody wanted this crossing to stop being possible

resolve.success: you learn who threw them and why, and it is the transgression in miniature
resolve.failure: you set one back up and whatever they were keeping out finds the line again
resolve.orElse: leave them down; you cross by luck, which runs out on the descent

decisions.cue: a hospice door barred from the inside with the bell cut down
decisions.cost: whoever is in there stopped answering

resolve.success: you talk them into opening and they have kept everything anybody left here
resolve.failure: you force it and what is inside was barred in, not out
resolve.orElse: leave it barred; the crossing is made without rest or news

decisions.cue: a track going into the pass with none at all coming out
decisions.cost: everything that went through is still in there

resolve.success: you read what went in and how long ago, and can time your crossing to miss it
resolve.failure: you go in behind it and catch it up in the narrows
resolve.orElse: go round the hill, costing a Turn and putting you on the wrong side at dark

situations.doing: standing at the top of the pass with the next one down
situations.onArrival: it is warm on the side out of the wind and the wind is not blowing
situations.because: the line is walked stone to stone and one is missing
situations.offer: set the fallen stone up and the whole crossing lets you through

situations.doing: ringing a bell that has been cut down
situations.onArrival: it moves the rope and no sound comes
situations.because: the bell is rung for whoever is on the crossing and there is no bell
situations.offer: give it a bell and it will shelter you, and everything else stays outside

situations.doing: waiting at a rockfall with stock they cannot move
situations.onArrival: they ask whether the far side is any clearer
situations.because: the pass closed with them on the wrong side of it
situations.offer: clear a line and they will drive you through anything on this hill

situations.doing: standing in the narrows facing the way out
situations.onArrival: it steps aside and then steps back
situations.because: the pass asks leave and it never gave any
situations.offer: ask leave aloud and it will let you and everything behind you through

situations.doing: standing open and empty with tracks going in and none out
situations.onArrival: the wind in it drops entirely as you come to the mouth
situations.because: it is the only way through and it likes being asked
situations.offer: ask it properly and it will be a road rather than a trap

situations.doing: hanging in a frame at the top of the crossing with the rope gone
situations.onArrival: it sounds once when the wind moves and not again
situations.because: it is rung to bring people in off the pass
situations.offer: ring it and everything still out on the crossing comes in

temptations.cue: the waystone from the top
temptations.benefit: once, always know which way is through
temptations.standingDrawback: the crossing has no top stone while you carry it, and closes

temptations.cue: a hand-bell that carries the crossing
temptations.benefit: once, be heard the whole length of the pass
temptations.standingDrawback: everything on the crossing hears it

temptations.cue: the hospice key
temptations.benefit: shelter at the top of the crossing
temptations.standingDrawback: you are the keeper now, and callers come

temptations.cue: leave asked and granted
temptations.benefit: once, pass anything that guards a way
temptations.standingDrawback: leave given can be withdrawn

temptations.cue: a drover's stock-stick
temptations.benefit: once, move something that will not move
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you move, the hill wants back at the bottom

weight.dangerLine: everything on this hill is on its way to the bottom and most of it has not started yet

institution: scree slopes that move a little every time anything crosses them
a corrie floor made entirely of what used to be above it
boulders standing where nothing else is, having stopped
ritual: a stone rolled down at the same place by everyone who passes
the avalanche ground crossed one at a time, never together
nothing carried down that was not carried up
demand: a boulder balanced with a clear run below it
a cornice overhanging with a crack behind it
scree with one line of prints across it and no more
wound: a whole slope come down at once onto the path
a corrie floor with something under it that was walking
boulders stacked by hands rather than fallen
anchor: a slope that has finished moving
a line across the scree that has held

features: a boulder balanced with a run below
a crack behind a cornice
one line of prints across scree
a slope come down onto a path
boulders stacked by hands
a stone that stopped rolling

decisions.cue: a boulder standing balanced with a clear run below it
decisions.cost: it is going down; the only question is when and onto what

resolve.success: you put it down deliberately, into nothing, and the slope settles for good
resolve.failure: you cross beneath it and it goes while you are under: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: go round above it, costing a Turn on ground that also moves

decisions.cue: a cornice overhanging the gully with a crack behind it
decisions.cost: it will not hold and the gully is the fast way down

resolve.success: you read the crack and take the buttress instead, and watch the cornice go behind you
resolve.failure: you take the gully and it comes off above you
resolve.orElse: wait for the cold to firm it, costing a Turn and a night out

decisions.cue: scree with one line of prints across it and nothing since
decisions.cost: one crossing held; a second might not

resolve.success: you cross one at a time on the same line and the slope holds for all of you
resolve.failure: you cross together and take the slope with you
resolve.orElse: go round the scree entirely, adding a Turn and putting you on the skyline

decisions.cue: a whole slope come down at once onto the path below
decisions.cost: there is something under it and it was recent

resolve.success: you find what is under it and get it out, and it is owed to somebody at the ending
resolve.failure: you dig and start the rest of the slope moving
resolve.orElse: leave it; whatever is under there is not accounted for and the ending is poorer

decisions.cue: boulders stacked by hands rather than fallen, in a line
decisions.cost: somebody built this and it is holding something back

resolve.success: you see what it holds back and can keep it holding
resolve.failure: you take one out to see and the line goes, and so does what it held
resolve.orElse: leave it; you never learn what somebody thought worth stacking against

decisions.cue: a stone lying at the foot of a slope that clearly stopped rolling short
decisions.cost: everything else went to the bottom and this did not

resolve.success: you understand why it stopped and can make one other thing stop too
resolve.failure: you move it and it resumes, immediately, taking the slope with it
resolve.orElse: leave it; nothing you set down on this hill stays where you put it

situations.doing: standing under a balanced boulder with its hands up
situations.onArrival: it has been holding the boulder and it is not holding the boulder
situations.because: it was under the slope when the slope came down
situations.offer: take the weight for a moment and it will step out and tell you everything

situations.doing: stacking boulders into a line, one at a time
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you can hear it moving yet
situations.because: he has been building against the slope for years
situations.offer: help him place one and he will tell you which ground will hold you

situations.doing: standing alone on a corrie floor with a clear run behind it
situations.onArrival: the ground around it is undisturbed and it is warm to touch
situations.because: it stopped rolling and nothing else here did
situations.offer: ask it how and it will hold whatever you need held

situations.doing: lying with one line of prints across it and nothing since
situations.onArrival: the whole slope shifts an inch as you set foot on it
situations.because: it moves when anything crosses and it has been crossed once
situations.offer: cross one at a time and the slope will hold for you every time after

situations.doing: digging at a slope that came down on the path
situations.onArrival: they dig with their hands and do not get anywhere
situations.because: there is somebody under it and there always has been
situations.offer: dig with them and what comes out is owed at the ending

situations.doing: overhanging a gully with a crack running behind it
situations.onArrival: snow slides off the lip while you are looking at it
situations.because: it is going to come off and it has not chosen when
situations.offer: bring it down on your terms and the gully is safe the whole way

temptations.cue: the stone that stopped rolling
temptations.benefit: once, make a thing stay where you put it
temptations.standingDrawback: everything else you have set down starts moving

temptations.cue: a wedge cut for a balanced boulder
temptations.benefit: once, hold back what is coming down
temptations.standingDrawback: it holds until you need it somewhere else

temptations.cue: a knowledge of which line holds
temptations.benefit: cross moving ground safely
temptations.standingDrawback: the line holds for you and not for those behind you

temptations.cue: a stone off the built line
temptations.benefit: once, know what a thing is holding back
temptations.standingDrawback: the line is one stone weaker

temptations.cue: a set of prints that held
temptations.benefit: once, follow ground that will take your weight
temptations.standingDrawback: they lead where the maker was going, not where you are
